claim: Did you know… distinctively Black names do not hurt life outcomes?

studies.cite: Fryer & Levitt (2004), Quarterly Journal of Economics
studies.finding: Using California birth records, the authors found no negative causal effect of a distinctively Black first name on later life outcomes once background was controlled.
studies.verdict: Conflicts with résumé audit studies; the picture remains contested.

claim: Did you know… the clock change makes judges hand down longer sentences?

studies.finding: Federal judges gave longer sentences on the Monday after the spring clock change, which the authors attributed to lost sleep.
studies.verdict: Seen as sensitive to the model used.

studies.finding: A reanalysis found the effect depended on control variables and was absent in data from 2004 to 2016.
studies.verdict: Comment disputes the result; original not confirmed.

claim: Did you know… violent video games make players more aggressive?

studies.finding: A meta-analysis of experimental, cross-sectional and longitudinal studies in Eastern and Western countries linked violent game play to higher aggression.
studies.verdict: Large literature, but effect size is disputed.

studies.finding: A meta-analysis of 101 studies of youth found a very small aggression effect, r = .06, and flagged publication bias.
studies.verdict: Smaller estimate; the two camps still disagree.

claim: Did you know… graffiti and litter in a neighbourhood lead to violent crime?

studies.cite: Sampson & Raudenbush (1999), American Journal of Sociology
studies.finding: Rating over 23,000 Chicago street segments, the authors found disorder and crime were correlated, but both tracked neighbourhood collective efficacy.
studies.verdict: Link between disorder and crime was largely spurious, except possibly robbery.
